tells: 1. The laugh barely builds: across 1 s only the woman in the white sweater lifts a hand to her mouth; the rest of the front tables keep the same pose and gaze, so the moment reads as a still with one animated figure rather than a room catching a line (club-5-strip.png, front tables, all six frames)

2. The candles on every table are the obvious motivated source, yet no face gets warm uplight or flicker from them; faces carry an even frontal fill from nowhere, so the light reads as CG rather than as the room (club-1-wide.png / club-2-mid.png, faces above the candle tables)

3. The face close's foreground and background figures are low-poly and faceted: the blonde at left has a polygonal neck and jaw, and a flat green-grey shard of shoulder crosses the lower centre. The camera's out-of-focus layer gives the render away at once (club-4-face.png, left third and lower centre)

4. The frame is badly unbalanced: the top 40% is crushed black with no ceiling or haze detail, and a hard-edged black rectangle (an occluder or the stage lip) sits in the lower centre-left foreground (club-1-wide.png and club-6-held.png, top band and lower centre-left 330-545 x 600-670)

5. The back of the house is a flat wall of identical dark standing silhouettes with no rim light or variation, and the wide and the held frame are near duplicates (same poses, same gazes), so the room looks static between cuts (club-1-wide.png vs club-6-held.png, back rows and front tables)
1. The front row sits in identical waiting-room postures, upright with both hands on the knees and feet together, like mannequins lined up for a photo (theatre-1-wide.png, front row lower centre)

2. Faces in the second and third rows are lit bright and flat while their bodies and the seats around them fall to black, so the heads read as floating pasted masks with no motivated key (theatre-2-mid.png / theatre-6-held.png, rows 2-3 upper half)

3. The faceted low-poly bodies in the face close: the shoulder at left is a polygonal slab with a red triangular shard at its edge, the right figure's jacket is plain blocky geometry, and the woman's eyes are glassy with a fixed catchlight (theatre-4-face.png, left and right thirds, eyes)

4. The back stalls are a grid of identical flat silhouette cut-outs at one height, with sparkling blue and white specks in the haze that shimmer like noise rather than practicals or phone screens (theatre-1-wide.png / theatre-5-strip.png, upper half; blue speck around 860,160 in theatre-2-mid.png)

5. Odd figures stand in the aisles at the edges of the wide, and a red glow smears the arm of a front-left spectator. Both look like placement and lighting bugs (theatre-1-wide.png at left 70-130 x 300-520 and right 1170-1220; theatre-3-mid.png at left 140-220 x 380-450)

1. The hair in the face close renders as a striped, aliased card mesh behind the ear, and a disembodied pale hand floats beside the blonde at right (openmic-4-face.png, 780-870 x 180-340 and 1090-1210 x 530-610)

2. The downlights are flat glowing discs that light nothing: no pools on the wall below them and no top light on hair or shoulders, while every face gets the same soft frontal fill. The key light has no source (openmic-1-wide.png / openmic-2-mid.png, ceiling row and faces)

3. The front row is packed shoulder into shoulder, with bodies and arms interpenetrating between neighbours (the green-top woman and the girl in black overlap, and arms cross into the next seat) (openmic-3-mid.png, centre 490-780 x 400-600; openmic-1-wide.png, front row)
4. A hard vertical seam runs down the curly-haired man's hair or hat, and his hairline is a solid helmet with no strand breakup (openmic-2-mid.png, 280-300 x 225-270)

5. The wide is flat and boxy: a crushed black ceiling band, a featureless tan door slab at left, and a bare back wall make it read as a game room rather than a lived-in venue, and the faces show no shadow modelling (openmic-1-wide.png, top third and left 195-250 x 250-350)
